summary: This is a whitepaper/token sale document by VitaDAO for VITA-FAST Molecules, ERC-20 tokens representing fractions of the "Discovering Novel Autophagy Activators" IP-NFT funding the Korolchuk Lab at Newcastle University. The project focuses on identifying novel autophagy activators using cell-based screening assays, with Niemann-Pick Type C (NPC) as the disease model. The document describes the research background, experimental plan, current status (initial screening completed, second-generation compound screening in progress), tokenomics, and future clinical development pathway.

content_blocks.title: Executive Summary
content_blocks.content: VitaDAO is funding the Korolchuk Lab at Newcastle University to discover novel autophagy activators. VITA-FAST tokens (ERC-20 on Ethereum) represent fractions of the IP-NFT covering this research. Token holders receive governance rights over IP generated by the lab. Total of 1,000,000 VITA-FAST tokens minted. Token issued in compliance with Swiss law; not available to U.S. persons. Risks include unpredictable research outcomes, regulatory changes, and IP enforcement challenges.

content_blocks.title: Project Overview
content_blocks.content: VitaDAO owns IP rights to research into autophagy activators by the Korolchuk Lab at Newcastle University. The lab focuses on molecular mechanisms controlling cellular homeostasis and aging, identifying therapeutic targets for age-related diseases. Led by Dr. Viktor Korolchuk (expert in autophagy and lysosomal biology). VitaDAO initially supported the lab via a Sponsored Research Agreement (SRA) to fund investigations into cellular mechanisms of aging and drug discovery. The sale of VITA-FAST tokens aims to continue supporting this work and empower community governance of longevity therapeutics development.

content_blocks.title: Project Background – Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content: Aging is associated with decline in autophagy capacity. Autophagy is a cell's 'waste-management' system: it sequesters, degrades, and recycles faulty cellular components (dysfunctional organelles, misfolded proteins, defective DNA, ROS). Impaired autophagy is linked to neurodegenerative disorders: Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Huntington's, ALS. The project focuses on lysosomal autophagy activators. Niemann-Pick Type C (NPC) was chosen as the disease model because it is a monogenetic orphan disease with better-understood biology and a shorter path to drug approval. Therapeutics developed could extend to other lysosomal storage disorders and diseases with lysosomal dysfunction (Alzheimer's, Parkinson's).

content_blocks.title: Mechanism of Faulty Autophagy Leading to Cell Death (Prior Contribution by Dr. Korolchuk)
content_blocks.content: Dr. Korolchuk previously contributed to establishing the mechanism by which faulty autophagy leads to cell death: (1) Dysfunctional mitochondria accumulate due to inadequate recycling by faulty autophagy; (2) Accumulation of ROS and DNA damage induces cellular stress; (3) Stress response pathways activated (PARP & SIRT); (4) Depletion of NAD+ and NADH essential to cellular metabolic pathways; (5) Mitochondria lose ability to generate ATP as they become depolarized; (6) Apoptosis begins. This represents completed prior research establishing mechanistic foundation.

content_blocks.title: Experimental Design and Assay System
content_blocks.content: Disease model: Npc1 -/- cells (mutation in lysosomal protein Niemann-Pick C1) subjected to metabolic stress → cell death due to dysfunctional autophagy. Readout: cells dead/cells alive. Control: Atg5 -/- cells (lack autophagy initiation, not rescuable by autophagy inducers) used in parallel to differentiate true autophagy activators from non-specific cell survival compounds. Compound library: ~4,000 bioactive molecules and commercial small molecules. Natural compounds from KVP lab (plant and animal origin, high bioavailability for drug translation). Experimental plan: (1) Assay optimization and screening in cell survival assays (Atg5-/- vs Npc1-/-) with dose-response, using mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs); (2) Luciferase-p62 clearance assay; (3) Halo orthogonal assay; (4) Selection and purchase of lead series derivatives; (5) Screening of commercial derivatives in cell survival, p62 clearance, and Halo assays; (6) Synthesis of lead series at CRO and mechanism of action determination; (7) SAR and validation in vitro autophagy assays.

content_blocks.title: Assay Descriptions
content_blocks.content: Cell survival assay: Screens bioactive and commercial small molecules to identify which can reactivate autophagy in NPC1 -/- cells. Also filters out cytotoxic compounds. Luciferase-p62 clearance assay: Generation and optimization of Npc1 -/- MEFs with inducible tet-on-tet-off expression of luciferase-tagged autophagy flux reporter p62. Clearance of p62 protein is only possible with proper autophagy; quantifying clearance confirms autophagy occurrence and level. Halo-GFP-LC3 orthogonal assay: Npc1 -/- cells stably expressing 'traffic-light' EGFP-RFP-LC3 for high-throughput high-content screening. Automated image analysis provides number of autophagosomes, autolysosomes, and whether autophagy has been activated.

content_blocks.title: Project Status and Future Plans
content_blocks.content: Current status: Data generated on thousands of compounds from initial library using described assays. Several compounds identified with potential autophagic properties. Lead series identified; library of derivatives classified and synthesized by external suppliers. Screened small molecules have high chemical variability and no similarity to pre-existing autophagy inducers — representing high possibility of novel IP. At time of publishing: lab is screening second generation of compounds developed as lead series based on hits; awaiting delivery of additional chemical series of leads. These derivatives will undergo same screening (cell survival, p62 clearance, autolysosome quantification). Future: Once lead molecules identified, VitaDAO and Molecule will work with Newcastle University on drug translation (pharmacokinetics, target deconvolution, SAR, scalability, manufacturing). Further in vitro and in vivo research planned: NPC patient-derived fibroblasts, CRISPR-Cas9 Npc1 KO cells, iPSCs, Npc1-mutant mice and cats.

content_blocks.title: Clinical Development Pathway (Planned)
content_blocks.content: Phase 1 Clinical Trials: Small group (20-100) healthy volunteers or patients; evaluate safety, dosage, side effects. Phase 2 Clinical Trials: For NPC, Orphan Drug designation could be sought (tax credits, FDA user fee waiver). Phase 3 Clinical Trials: If successful in NPC, drug could be tried for Alzheimer's disease as future indication (own full clinical trials required). FDA Review and Market: NDA submitted post-Phase 3; FDA review up to 2 years (faster with Breakthrough Therapy designation). All clinical stages are future/planned with no dates specified.

content_blocks.title: Blockchain, NFTs, IP-NFTs, and Molecules – Technology Framework
content_blocks.content: IP-NFTs attach legal contracts (e.g., sponsored research agreements) to smart contracts (NFTs) on Ethereum. They can be transferred peer-to-peer, made composable with DeFi, used to distribute governance to stakeholders, and create liquidity in IP markets. First IP-NFTs minted by Molecule for VitaDAO to register longevity therapeutics IP and R&D data rights on Ethereum. Molecules (VITA-FAST) represent membership in an IP pool containing IP and R&D data attached to the parent IP-NFT. Governance rights, IP access, duty of care, and confidentiality obligations are defined in the Korolchuk-Free Association of Molecules (FAM) Membership Agreement.

content_blocks.title: Tokenomics of VITA-FAST
content_blocks.content: Total supply: 1,000,000 VITA-FAST tokens. Distribution: 10% (100,000) sold in genesis sale to max 499 VITA tokenholders (2-month vesting, 2-month cliff); 69% retained by VitaDAO (liquid); 5% to Researchers (vested 4 years, 1-year cliff); 1% to Newcastle University (vested 4 years, 1-year cliff); 5% to VitaDAO dealflow working group contributors (vested 4 years, 1-year cliff, subject to VitaDAO governance approval); 10% to liquidity pool (Uniswap V3, matched with 10% of funds raised). Rights: Governance (voting on licenses and use of proceeds), Access to IP/R&D data (for due diligence, no license granted), Duty of Care, Confidentiality.

content_blocks.title: Genesis Sale Structure and Valuation
content_blocks.content: Fixed-price sale with pro rata distribution, overflow refunds, and 2-month vesting. Funds raised in wrapped ether (WETH). Cost-based valuation: Research costs 220,358 CHF (245,557 USD) + legal/operational costs 38,563 CHF (43,295 USD) + inflation 23,865 USD = total 312,717 USD for all 1,000,000 tokens. 10% of tokens valued at 31,271 USD; price of 0.31271 USD per VITA-FAST token. Sale period: 2 days. Bidders must lock (stake) VITA equivalent to ETH bid amount. If sales goal not met, all funds returned. Pro rata distribution if goal met or exceeded. Overflow automatically returned via smart contract. 2-month (60-day) vesting; participants receive vVITA and vVITA-FAST during vesting.

Alice bids 15 ETH + 15,000 VITA → claims 750 vVITA-FAST + 12,000 vVITA + refund of 3 ETH + 3,000 VITA → unlocks 750 VITA-FAST + 12,000 VITA. Timeline: SALE (2 DAYS) → VESTING (60 DAYS) → UNLOCK.

content_blocks.title: Use of Funds
content_blocks.content: Immediate use: Establish liquidity for VITA-FAST (Uniswap V3 pool). Subsequent use governed by VITA-FAST token holders. Example uses: (1) Decentralized SAR analysis via LabDAO network of computational chemists and hackathons; (2) Engaging experienced medicinal chemists; (3) Filing patents for novel compounds generated by research. Transition from liquidity to IP generation should be a community decision.

content_blocks.title: Risk Factors
content_blocks.content: Key risks identified: Liquidity Risk (limited market for Molecules); Regulatory Risk (evolving landscape for blockchain/digital assets); Project Risk (research success not guaranteed, delays, cost overruns, unexpected results); Technological Risk (hacking, technical glitches, blockchain issues); Smart Contract Risk (bugs or security vulnerabilities); Market Risk (value fluctuation due to NFT/biotech IP/crypto market changes); Intellectual Property Risk (disputes or uncertainties in IP ownership/enforcement); Legal and Compliance Risk (tax liabilities by jurisdiction); Network Risk (Ethereum network changes, forks, congestion); Operational Risk (platform downtime); Governance Risk (disagreements among token holders).

content_blocks.title: Legal Considerations
content_blocks.content: VITA-FAST represents membership in IP pool containing the Discovering Novel Autophagy Activators IP-NFT. Token holders may govern: (1) issuance of licenses to use underlying IP/R&D data; (2) proceeds from licensing or sale of IP/R&D data (not hard-coded; requires careful judgment and legal advice). Information rights: regular non-confidential updates, access to data rooms (open non-confidential room + confidential room requiring KYC and NDA). VITA-FAST will NOT be sold to U.S. persons (Regulation S of Securities Act of 1933); enforcement via IP address checks, geofencing, and attestations. Issued in compliance with Swiss law.

content_blocks.title: Team
content_blocks.content: Viktor Korolchuk: Cell biologist, leads Korolchuk Lab at Newcastle University. PhD from University of Cambridge (2007); postdoctoral positions at UC San Diego and University of Cambridge. Research: molecular mechanisms of cellular homeostasis, neurodegenerative diseases, cancer. Funding from UK Medical Research Council, European Research Council, Wellcome Trust. Member of Biochemical Society and Royal Society of Biology. Peter Banks: Geneticist, PhD from Newcastle University (cohesins in C. elegans). Postdoctoral with David Lydall (chromatin modifications in budding yeast). Appointed 2011 to run high-throughput screening facility at Newcastle University Faculty of Medical Sciences. Developed mammalian siRNA screening (2012). Jóhannes Reynisson: Drug discovery expert, research lead at VitaDAO. PhD in chemical biology from University of Copenhagen. Experience at Novartis, AstraZeneca, Institute of Cancer Research (London), University of Auckland (NZ). 150+ peer-reviewed publications and patents. Focus: drug candidates for cancer, infectious diseases, neurodegenerative disorders.

key_findings: Research is at early drug discovery stage (TRL 2-3): initial compound library screening completed on thousands of compounds using cell-based assays (Npc1-/- vs Atg5-/- MEFs), with several lead series identified.
Second-generation compound screening is in progress at time of publication; derivatives synthesized by external suppliers and awaiting delivery.

Three orthogonal assay systems established: cell survival assay (Npc1-/- MEFs), luciferase-p62 clearance assay, and Halo-GFP-LC3 high-content imaging assay — providing multi-parameter confirmation of autophagy activation.
Screened small molecules have high chemical variability and no similarity to pre-existing autophagy inducers, representing high possibility of novel IP.
Disease model: Niemann-Pick Type C (NPC, monogenetic orphan disease) chosen for shorter regulatory path; potential future indications include Alzheimer's and Parkinson's.
No in vivo data reported yet; in vivo models (Npc1-mutant mice and cats) are planned for future stages.
No clinical data; full clinical development pathway (Phase 1-3, NDA) is planned but not initiated.
VitaDAO owns IP rights via Sponsored Research Agreement (SRA) with Newcastle University; IP registered as IP-NFT on Ethereum.
Total research costs committed: 220,358 CHF (245,557 USD); legal/operational costs: 38,563 CHF (43,295 USD).

Team includes experienced researchers: Dr. Korolchuk (autophagy/lysosomal biology expert, funded by MRC, ERC, Wellcome Trust), Peter Banks (high-throughput screening), Jóhannes Reynisson (drug discovery, 150+ publications).
No patents filed yet; patent filing for novel compounds is listed as a potential future use of funds.
VITA-FAST token sale target: 31,271 USD (10% of 1,000,000 tokens at 0.31271 USD/token).
